---
title: "Instructor Guide"
subtitle: "How to run, update, and archive Beyond Downloading"
---

This guide is for anyone teaching the course. The [lessons](../lessons/01-apis.qmd) contain everything learners see. The pages here add preparation steps, teaching notes, and known problems.

## The teaching rhythm

Each session has two halves:

1.  **🖥️ Slides**: concepts, ground rules, and a tour of the data sources.
2.  **👀 Live demo**: switch to your editor and run the demo file one chunk at a time. Learners run the same chunks in their own copy.

## Live coding tips

-   **Run one chunk at a time** and talk about the output before moving on.
-   **Use a big font** and a light color theme for the projector.
-   **Read errors out loud** and fix them together. Learners will meet the same errors.
-   **Expect live sites to misbehave.** APIs time out and web pages change. Treat a failure as a teaching moment about why we save snapshots and log provenance.

## Before the course

-   **One week before:** send learners the [Setup](../setup.qmd) page. Remind them that the Census key can take a few minutes to arrive, and that it must go in `.Renviron` before Lesson 1.
-   **The day before each session:** run the whole demo file yourself. Websites and APIs change, so a demo that worked last term may not work now. See the session pages for the parts most likely to break.
-   **Before each session:** have your own Census key loaded and the Playwright example working, in case the network is slow.

## Session overview

| Session | Lesson | Time | Slides | Demo file |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | [APIs](session-01.qmd) | 120 min | `APIs/APIs.qmd` | `APIs/API_demonstration.qmd` |
| 2 | [Web scraping](session-02.qmd) | 120 min | `web_scraping/web_scraping.qmd` | `web_scraping/web_scraping_demonstration.qmd`, `web_scraping/scraping_using_playwright.py` |

Each session is planned for about 120 minutes: slides first, then the live demo.

## The materials

| File or folder | What's in it |
|---|---|
| `index.qmd`, `pages/` | The website pages (home, setup, lessons, resources, archive, this guide) |
| `APIs/`, `web_scraping/` | The slides and demo files for each lesson |
| `archive/` | Copies of past slides, linked from the [Archive](../archive.qmd) page |
| `_quarto.yml` | Website settings: navigation, sidebar, theme |
| `docs/` | The rendered website. GitHub Pages serves this folder, so don't edit it by hand |

## Updating the website

1.  Edit the `.qmd` files.
2.  In the terminal, from the course folder, run:

    ``` bash
    quarto render
    ```

    This rebuilds the whole site, including the slides, into `docs/`.

3.  Commit and push, **including `docs/`**. GitHub Pages updates a minute or two later.

To preview while you edit, run `quarto preview` instead. It opens the site in your browser and reloads when you save.

::: callout-note
The site shows the demo code without running it (`eval: false` in `_quarto.yml`), because the demos call live websites and the Census API needs a key. Learners run the code themselves.
:::

## Archiving the slides at the end of a term

Before you change the slides for a new term, save a copy of the current ones:

1.  Run `quarto render` so `docs/` has the latest slides.
2.  Make a folder for the term, for example `archive/2026-fall/`.
3.  Copy `docs/APIs/APIs.html` and `docs/web_scraping/web_scraping.html` into it. The slides are self-contained (`embed-resources: true`), so each one is a single file.
4.  On the [Archive](../archive.qmd) page (`pages/archive.qmd`), change the links in that term's row to point to the copies, for example `../archive/2026-fall/APIs.html`, and add a new row for the new term.
5.  Render, commit, and push.
